assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational explanation of how collateral constraints amplify credit cycles and macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki, Gertler, and Moore provide the central theoretical contributions, although related financial-accelerator work has a wider literature.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established, extensively used in macroeconomic modelling, and highly relevant to recurrent financial instability.
uncertainties: The precise boundary between the collateral and financial-accelerator strands requires careful prize-definition work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework transformed the analysis and conduct of modern monetary policy.
assessment.attribution: Calvo, Woodford, and Taylor are central contributors, but the contribution is unusually cumulative and includes several other indispensable researchers.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been tested through decades of central-bank practice, empirical work, and macroeconomic research.
uncertainties: Attribution is difficult because the listed contribution encompasses a broad multi-author research programme.
A three-person prize cannot fully represent all major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a durable new account of trade patterns and the gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the clearest originator of the canonical heterogeneous-firm trade framework; Helpman and Redding made major linked contributions.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply integrated into trade theory and empirical work and has influenced policy analysis.
uncertainties: The appropriate scope of a prize between the core model and its broader research programme remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation programme gave a powerful quantitative account of productivity and income differences across countries.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Restuccia, and Klenow are directly associated with the leading measurement and quantitative formulations.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has generated a substantial empirical and theoretical literature over many years.
uncertainties: Estimated misallocation and causal mechanisms can be sensitive to modelling and measurement assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models materially improved analysis of policy transmission, household balance sheets, and distributional effects.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante are central to the modern synthesis represented by this candidate.
assessment.maturity: The framework is influential in contemporary macroeconomics and policy institutions, with a growing body of quantitative applications.
uncertainties: The research programme is comparatively recent relative to the oldest prize-worthy traditions.
Its eventual empirical and policy robustness remains under continuing evaluation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and made inequality of opportunity more concretely analyzable.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are leading contributors to the core research programme, with Katz also an important collaborator.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been replicated, extended, and extensively used in research and public debate.
uncertainties: The interpretation of mobility measures and their policy implications remains contested.
Credit allocation within the broader administrative-data programme is not straightforward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on tasks, technology, and trade shocks reshaped understanding of labour-market polarization and regional adjustment.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson have made distinct and closely connected core contributions; Katz is also important to the wider literature.
assessment.maturity: The work has accumulated influential evidence and generated a large literature on labour-market adjustment.
uncertainties: Separating the effects of technology, trade, and other coincident economic changes remains empirically challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Decision theory under ambiguity supplied fundamental alternatives to expected utility for analysing choice with poorly specified probabilities.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa and Epstein are especially central to the canonical maxmin formulation, while Marinacci made major contributions to the broader theory.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical contribution is long established and influential across decision theory, finance, and economic modelling.
uncertainties: The empirical distinctiveness and comparative descriptive success of competing ambiguity models remain unsettled.
